subject: anatomy
title: Gastrointestinal Tract Histology and Hepatic Architecture

steps.tx: The gastrointestinal tract exhibits a fundamental four-layered wall architecture consisting of mucosa, submucosa, muscularis externa, and serosa or adventitia. The **esophagus** is lined by a thick nonkeratinised stratified squamous epithelium designed to withstand mechanical food bolus abrasion. Its muscularis externa exhibits a unique regional transition: striated skeletal muscle in the upper third, mixed in the middle third, and purely smooth muscle in the lower third.
steps.say: The gut tube shares a four-layered wall comprising mucosa, submucosa, muscularis, and serosa. The esophagus is lined by nonkeratinised stratified squamous epithelium to resist bolus friction. Its muscular wall shifts from skeletal muscle in the upper third to smooth muscle in the lower third.

vis.caption: Gastrointestinal wall stratification and glandular specializations. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: At the gastroesophageal junction (Z-line), the stratified squamous epithelium abruptly transforms into simple columnar epithelium. The gastric mucosa features gastric pits opening into tubular gastric glands. The acid-secreting **parietal cell** (oxyntic cell) resides predominantly in the body and fundus, distinguished by extensive intracellular canaliculi and abundant mitochondria that power hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor secretion.
steps.say: At the gastroesophageal junction, stratified squamous epithelium abruptly becomes simple columnar. In the gastric body, acid-secreting parietal cells feature intracellular canaliculi and dense mitochondria that drive hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor production.

left.title: Parietal (Oxyntic) Cells
points: Located in upper and middle gland neck
Intensely eosinophilic pyramidal cells
Secretes hydrochloric acid (HCl)
Secretes intrinsic factor for B12 absorption

right.title: Chief (Peptic) Cells
points: Located at the deep glandular base
Basophilic cytoplasm packed with zymogen
Secretes inactive pepsinogen proenzyme
Stimulated by vagal acetylcholine and acid

steps.tx: Located in the deep base of gastric glands are **chief cells**, which synthesize and store the proenzyme pepsinogen inside apical zymogen granules. Mucous neck cells secrete protective soluble mucin, while enteroendocrine G cells in the pyloric antrum secrete gastrin into the bloodstream to stimulate parietal acid secretion.
steps.say: Chief cells sit in the glandular base, storing pepsinogen in apical zymogen granules. Mucous neck cells produce protective mucus, while enteroendocrine G cells in the pyloric antrum secrete gastrin to stimulate parietal acid production.

steps.tx: The small intestine amplifies absorptive surface area through plicae circulares, intestinal villi, and brush-border microvilli. The duodenum is uniquely characterized by branched coiled **Brunner glands** packed within its submucosa. These submucosal glands secrete alkaline mucin rich in bicarbonate to neutralize acidic gastric chyme entering from the pylorus.
steps.say: The small bowel multiplies its surface area through plicae circulares, villi, and microvilli. The duodenum is identified by branched Brunner glands filling its submucosa. These glands secrete alkaline bicarbonate-rich fluid to neutralize acidic stomach chyme.

left.title: Duodenum Histology
points: Extensive branched Brunner glands in submucosa
Leaf-like broad intestinal villi
Receives bile and pancreatic secretions
Neutralizes acidic peptic chyme

right.title: Ileum Histology
points: Massive Peyer patches in antimesenteric wall
Shorter finger-like intestinal villi
High density of mucus goblet cells
Absorbs vitamin B12 and bile salts

steps.tx: Between the bases of adjacent villi lie the simple tubular **crypts of Lieberkuhn**. In their deep bases reside zinc-rich Paneth cells, containing coarse eosinophilic granules packed with lysozyme, defensins, and phospholipase A2 to maintain antimicrobial defense of the gut mucosal barrier.
steps.say: Between the bases of villi sit the crypts of Lieberkuhn. Their bases house Paneth cells containing bright eosinophilic granules filled with lysozyme and defensins to maintain antimicrobial defenses against luminal pathogens.

nodes.label: Lgr5+ Basal Stem Cells in Crypt

steps.tx: In the distal ileum, the lamina propria and submucosa pack with prominent unencapsulated lymphoid aggregates designated **Peyer patches**, located along the antimesenteric border. The colon lacks villi entirely, presenting a flat mucosal surface perforated by straight tubular crypts densely crowded with mucus-secreting goblet cells to lubricate dehydrated fecal transit.
steps.say: In the distal ileum, the antimesenteric submucosa houses Peyer patches. The colon lacks villi, displaying a flat mucosal surface lined by straight crypts densely packed with goblet cells that lubricate the passage of solid stool.

steps.tx: The liver is organized into hexagonal **classical liver lobules** centred upon a terminal hepatic venule (central vein). At the periphery of each lobule sits the portal triad, comprising a branch of the portal vein, a branch of the hepatic artery, and an interlobular bile duct, wrapped in a connective tissue sleeve.
steps.say: The liver is structured into hexagonal classical lobules centred upon a central vein. At the lobule corners lie portal triads, each containing a portal venule, hepatic arteriole, and bile ductule wrapped in connective tissue.

steps.tx: Blood flows through fenestrated hepatic sinusoids past hepatocyte plates into the central vein. Separating the sinusoidal endothelium from hepatocytes is the subendothelial **Space of Disse**, containing microvilli for plasma exchange and hepatic stellate cells (Ito cells). Ito cells store vitamin A in quiescence, but transform into collagen-producing myofibroblasts during liver cirrhosis.
steps.say: Blood flows through fenestrated sinusoids toward the central vein. The Space of Disse separates endothelium from hepatocytes, housing Ito cells that store vitamin A. In chronic injury, Ito cells transdifferentiate into myofibroblasts that drive liver fibrosis.

left.title: Kupffer Cells
points: Resident liver macrophages in sinusoidal lumen
Derived from circulating monocytes
Phagocytose bacteria and spent red blood cells
Line sinusoidal endothelial walls

right.title: Hepatic Stellate (Ito) Cells
points: Reside in perisinusoidal Space of Disse
Primary storage depot for fat-soluble vitamin A
Activated by cytokines during chronic hepatitis
Chief cellular source of cirrhotic collagen scar
